title: Medullary development, catecholamines and the PNMT rule
guide: Medulla = neuroectoderm (20%), cortex = mesoderm (80%); complete by day 45 IUL. Catecholamines pulsatile, 80/20 adrenaline/NA; smaller granules adrenaline, larger dense NA. Metabolites (easier to measure): metanephrine/VMA, HVA, normetanephrine. Synthesis: tyrosine →(tyrosine hydroxylase, rate-limiting) DOPA → dopamine → NE →(PNMT) epinephrine. PNMT adrenal-only → extra-adrenal pheo makes only NE; cortisol stimulates PNMT.

title: Adrenomedullin and the pheochromocytoma types tree
guide: Adrenomedullin (endothelium): vasodilation, inhibits endothelial apoptosis (prevents septic shock); granules also contain opioids, chromogranin A. Pheo: 4th–5th decade, M=F; neural-crest tumour making catecholamines + metabolites. Adrenal 75% vs extra-adrenal paraganglioma 25% (high malignant potential; sympathetic 20% organ of Zuckerkandl; parasympathetic 5% non-functional carotid body > jugular bulb). Rule of 10 obsolete; current bilateral 40/extra-adrenal 25/familial 40/malignant 50. Familial: MEN strongest, VHL, NF-1; B/L except NF-1. Malignancy: metastasis surest; SDH-B ↑ metastatic potential. Book conflict: p853 tree labels vs p852 PNMT mechanism.

title: Pathophysiology, the triad and BP patterns
guide: Sustained sympathetic activity → ↑ intravascular volume (↓GFR → hypercalcaemia → acute abdominal pain; postural hypotension), DM, weight loss; EPO → 2° paraneoplastic polycythaemia. Triad: episodic headache 95% (m/c symptom), palpitation/tachycardia, profuse sweating. Others: abdominal pain, perspiration, panic attack 75%, pallor (suspect malignancy), weight loss, hyperadrenergic spells. Signs: episodic HTN 75–85% (m/c sign; sustained only 20% = resistant young HTN), normal BP 15%, postural hypotension 75% (↑HR >30/min, ↓SBP >20, ↓DBP >10).

title: Incidentaloma alarms, cardiac effects, histology and pre-test drugs
guide: Benign m/c; functional cortisol-producing > pheo. Non-functioning alarms (any 1 → adrenalectomy): >4 cm, CT >20 HU, washout <40%. Heart ↑ rate/excitability/O2/force; dilated cardiomyopathy (other: sarcoidosis). Hypercalcaemia associates: Addison's, pheo, thyrotoxicosis, acromegaly. m/c cause of panic attack is NOT pheo. Zellballen pattern; markers chromogranin, synaptophysin, S100. Stop TCAs, L-Dopa, NSAIDs before testing.

title: Screening, imaging and pre-operative preparation
guide: Screening: 24 hr fractionated metanephrine/NM (98%/98%); plasma 100% sensitivity (with urine if strong family history). MRI abdomen IOC (T2 hyperintense, hemorrhagic/cystic); MIBG/FDG-PET obsolete; Ga-DOTATATE PET IOC if MRI −ve but biochemically +ve (SSTR2 binding). TOC laparoscopic retroperitoneal adrenalectomy. 10 days before: admit + liberal fluids + α-blockade (phenoxybenzamine DOC, non-selective irreversible non-competitive; prazosin/terazosin; CCB if needed; metyrosine rarely); 3 days before: β-blocker atenolol; intraop crisis: sodium nitroprusside/nicardipine.
